title: 12a · Verify email before platform code access and agent handoff
body:
## Problem and outcome

A visitor should be able to browse, search, compare and try games immediately. Before they obtain code through HeadStart or request a reuse handoff to their coding agent, require a verified email and a valid session. After verification, resume the exact selected bag and intended action so the user does not have to rebuild their selection.

This follows the user's current instruction and supersedes earlier PRD statements allowing anonymous platform code exports where those conflict. It does not introduce a paywall, player accounts or a marketing subscription.

## Priority and dependencies

- Sequence: 12a; priority: P0; phase: Local reuse.
- Depends on: `catalog-api` (05) and `game-brief-collections` (08).
- This issue must pass before dependent implementation exposes platform-controlled code export or reuse handoff without this gate. Independent catalog research and public discovery can continue.
- Verify prerequisite behavior and data contracts independently before dependent implementation. An unrelated pending final mockup selection does not block this functional boundary.

## Scope and boundaries

Keep browse, search, public catalog metadata, external demos and public upstream source links open. Keep a local anonymous collection and editable brief available. Public upstream GitHub/Gitea/GitLab repositories remain publicly accessible under their own access rules; do not imply that HeadStart email verification restricts access to those upstream sources.

Require the server to validate a verified-email identity and live session before HeadStart-controlled code downloads, source-content exports, selected-source packages and reuse handoffs. Apply the same authorization policy to direct API requests, generated download URLs and MCP reuse operations. `search_components` and metadata-only `get_component` remain public; any endpoint that returns actual source content uses the code-access policy regardless of its name. Gate `prepare_handoff` when it creates a reuse/code-access artifact. A local agent's existing editing permissions are not globally controlled by a HeadStart account: editing code already present in the user's workspace remains governed by the user's local authorization.

Implement minimal passwordless verification using one coherent approach: a magic link or email OTP. Provide an adapter for localhost delivery preview so the complete flow can be exercised locally without configuring a hosted email provider or sending live email. Do not create provider accounts, configure domains or initiate live email delivery as part of this backlog-authoring task.

Authentication proves email control only. It does not resolve code/asset rights, grant integration authorization, create royalty agreements or bypass source-scope review gates.

## Implementation requirements

- Enforce the gate in a shared server authorization policy; client UI visibility, user-supplied `verified_email` fields and model assertions are insufficient. Derive verification from trusted server state and check session revocation before protected work or delivery.
- Verification challenges are random, single-use, purpose-bound and short-lived. Store only a secure token verifier/hash, expire challenges, cap attempts and consume them atomically. Bind completion to the intended email/challenge and prevent challenge substitution or replay.
- For OTPs, address their limited entropy with a keyed verifier, strict attempt limits and resend/issue throttles. For links, use a sufficiently unpredictable token and a configured canonical origin. Do not log tokens, codes, authentication URLs or credential-bearing request bodies.
- Use a server-owned or signed allowlist of relative return intents; reject arbitrary schemes, external origins and protocol-relative redirects. Never accept an arbitrary client redirect. Store only the minimal bag reference/revision and intended action needed to resume; retain local selections across the verification journey without leaking the bag or token to third parties.
- Establish sessions using secure, HttpOnly cookies with an explicit SameSite/CSRF policy, bounded lifetime, rotation after verification and logout/revocation. HTTPS is required in hosted environments; any loopback-only development exception must be explicit and fail closed outside localhost.
- Rate-limit challenge creation, resends, verification attempts and protected artifact generation. Responses must avoid exposing whether an email is already registered. Add request size limits and expected error responses without revealing session or verification details.
- For MCP, use a supported client authorization mechanism tied to the same verified server identity and authorization policy. Do not ask the model/user to paste email OTPs, magic links or session cookies into prompts. Keep catalog retrieval distinct from permission for local writes.
- Protected downloads must remain protected after creation: re-check authorization at delivery or use narrowly scoped, short-lived download capabilities issued only after verification. Catalog metadata must not leak unprotected generated code-export URLs.
- Model anonymous, challenge-issued, verification-failed/expired, verified, revoked and unavailable-delivery states explicitly. Verification must survive accidental navigation without losing the selected bag; resume only after success and re-check the bag revision, code rights and target action.
- Collect only the email and minimal account/session records required for access. Show the purpose clearly. No newsletter/marketing consent is implied by verification, and no marketing subscription is created.
- Keep auth UI components and tokens adaptable. Follow the currently selected baseline in `docs/design-direction.md` and issue #26; design the new verification states consistently with that baseline and identify the exact reference/version in review.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An anonymous user can browse, search, open allowed public metadata, launch an external demo, follow public repository links and maintain a local collection without login.
- [ ] Platform-controlled code export/download and reuse handoff requests require verified email on the server, including direct requests that bypass the UI and equivalent MCP operations.
- [ ] A crafted client verification flag, missing session, unverified identity, expired session and revoked session are all rejected before source artifacts are generated or returned.
- [ ] One-time link/OTP verification works end to end through the local delivery-preview adapter; expired, incorrect, exhausted, superseded and reused challenges fail safely, including concurrent replay attempts.
- [ ] Return destinations reject open redirects, challenge/session data stays out of logs, and cookie/CSRF/session rotation settings are tested for the selected implementation.
- [ ] The exact anonymous bag selection and intended action resume after verification, with revision/rights revalidation; cancel/error/retry paths preserve the selection without manufacturing success.
- [ ] Protected artifacts cannot be retrieved through a reusable public link or a metadata endpoint that bypasses the gate.
- [ ] MCP public search/metadata remains available, while reuse handoff requires the verified identity. Account verification does not trigger or authorize local filesystem edits.
- [ ] Rate limits and non-enumerating responses are exercised for sign-in issuance, resends and verification attempts; no live email is required for these tests.
- [ ] A localhost setup command and a documented development-only email preview are provided, with an explicit hosted-delivery adapter seam and no dependency on production provider credentials.
- [ ] Desktop/mobile browser evidence covers entry from a selected bag, challenge entry/sent state, expired/invalid state, successful resumption, logout and keyboard navigation. Reduced viewport behavior, focus and accessible error announcements pass independent critique.
- [ ] Independent coder and critical reviewer evidence identifies the reviewed commit/digest, actual tests and screenshots, findings and fixes. Functional/local criteria may pass against a clearly provisional visual reference and unblock specifically verified prerequisites. Under `docs/design-direction.md` and `docs/development-workflow.md`, pending required final visual acceptance keeps the overall issue open until the user-selected baseline is available and reviewed; desktop/mobile usability screenshots remain mandatory now.

## Verification and coder/reviewer loop

Assign a coder subagent to implement and exercise the server gate and local verification flow, then a different critical reviewer to inspect actual server/client/MCP code, tests and desktop/mobile screenshots. The reviewer must attempt direct API and MCP bypasses, replay/expiry, redirect abuse, anonymous discovery and selected-bag resumption, not approve from the coder's summary. Fix blocking findings and repeat independent review until the issue's acceptance criteria pass. Record the review in `docs/reviews/` with the reviewed revision and explicit PASS or CHANGES REQUESTED. Record functional passes separately when useful. If required final visual acceptance is pending, retain CHANGES REQUESTED/open overall with the exact design-baseline blocker; do not close the issue or imply a provisional screenshot is final visual approval. Follow [design direction](https://github.com/lucasaerb/headstart/blob/main/docs/design-direction.md) and [development workflow](https://github.com/lucasaerb/headstart/blob/main/docs/development-workflow.md).

## Deferred

Hosted email-provider setup, production email delivery, passwords, social login, billing, player saves, marketing automation and generalized account management are outside this issue. Implement only the minimal identity, verification and session lifecycle needed for the code-access boundary.

## Source of direction

Current user instruction: simple email/login before platform code-grab/use actions, while browsing/shopping remains open. The preserved public-source-link distinction and local-agent write boundary follow HeadStart's catalog/integration separation. Apply this current instruction over conflicting historical no-auth export guidance; do not silently change public discovery into an account-required experience.
